text:
sara.sales: Hey team — Acme wants a POC this week. Can we spin up a short-lived API token they can use from their dev env? They need it by EOD.

matt.se: Quick Q: how long do they need it for? 48h, 7 days? Also do they need IP allowlist or just a token?

sara.sales: 7 days preferred. They might test from a CI runner (dynamic IPs) so IP allowlist is tricky. Would prefer an expiring token and a clear revocation step.

leo.eng: We can create a time-limited token scoped to only generation endpoints and embeddings. Recommend TTL=168h (7d) + webhook to notify CS 24h before expiry. For CI use, ephemeral tokens are best.

anya.cs: Can you add audit logging so we can show Acme what calls happened during the POC? They asked in the security questionnaire.

leo.eng: Yep — all POC tokens are tracked in audit logs. I can add a note that logs are retained for 90 days for this POC. Want me to create the token or handoff to you?

sara.sales: Please create it and share the short instructions for rotation/revoke so I can include in the handoff doc. Need the token ID and the revoke command.

leo.eng: Created a token stub (not the real secret): token_id=tok-poc-acme-2026-03. I posted the real token to Secrets Manager. Instructions below.

leo.eng: Revoke from CLI:
```bash
# revoke by id
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/admin/keys/revoke \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_API_TOKEN\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{\"key_id\":\"tok-poc-acme-2026-03\"}'
```

leo.eng: Or from Console: Admin > Keys > search \"tok-poc-acme-2026-03\" > Revoke. Revocation is immediate and invalidates existing sessions.

anya.cs: Can we set automatic revoke at end of POC + manual revoke on demand?

leo.eng: Yes — I set auto-expiry 7d from creation and enabled manual revoke. Also added a 24h expiry reminder to the CS webhook.

matt.se: For rotation during the POC (customer requests weekly rotation), recommend issuing a new token and updating the app config — two tokens can coexist during rollout. Use the same token_id prefix for traceability.

sara.sales: Perfect. Any blockers for handing off to Acme? Need to include instructions in the onboarding email.

leo.eng: Add these bullets to the email: 
- Token TTL: 7 days (auto-expire)
- Scope: read/write generation + embeddings only
- Logs: request-level audit for 90 days
- Revoke command (CLI + Console)
- Rotation: create new token, swap in config, then revoke old token
- If customer needs IP restriction, contact eng-ops for a scoped allowlist (may delay by 24h)

anya.cs: I'll draft the onboarding email and include the revoke/rotation snippets. Sara, loop me in when you send.

sara.sales: Thanks all — please mark the token as POC and set owner = sara.sales in the key metadata. I'll send the email once I have the console link. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Created token tok-poc-acme-2026-03, expiry 7 days from 1743209999. Audit logging enabled. Assigned owner sara.sales.

leo.eng: Follow-up: If Acme wants the token rotated automatically, we can set up a rotation job but it requires updating their CI to pull secrets from our Secrets Manager via short-lived session tokens (recommend for production). For POC, manual rotation is simpler.

matt.se: Noted. I'll prepare a short FAQ for the handoff: how to swap tokens, how to revoke, troubleshooting 401s.

sara.sales: Great — closing this thread. I'll ping if Acme requests IP allowlist or longer retention.
